summary_en.motivation: To bridge the gap between mesoscale defect/porosity and macroscale fatigue behavior in additively manufactured Ti-6Al-4V.
summary_en.method: A multiscale modeling framework is developed to correlate mesoscale and macroscale fatigue responses using finite element and crystal plasticity models.
summary_en.result: The framework successfully predicts fatigue life and elucidates the role of microstructure and defects across scales.
summary_en.validation: Validation is performed against experimental S-N data from literature or numerical benchmarks.

papers.title: Cryogenic Treatment of Ti-6Al-4V Alloys: A Review of Effects on Microstructure, Mechanical Properties, and Machining Performance
papers.abstract: Ti-6Al-4V is a widely used α+β titanium alloy recognized for its strength-to-weight ratio, corrosion resistance, and biocompatibility. However, challenges in machinability and tool wear limit its processing efficiency. Cryogenic treatment, particularly deep cryogenic exposure at −196 °C for 36 hours, has shown promise in enhancing alloy performance by modifying its microstructure. Notably, β-phase content is reduced from 8.1% to 5.6%, promoting α-phase transformation and structural stability. Mechanical properties improve, including a 10.6% increase in elongation, a 13.5% reduction in fracture area, and up to an 8.3% rise in uniform plastic deformation indicators of better ductility and toughness. Surface hardness also increases. In machining, cryogenic cooling extends coated tool life by 50–90%, lowers cutting temperature by up to 57.4%, and reduces surface roughness by over 70% compared to wet machining. These gains arise from reduced thermal load, delayed crack propagation, and improved chip morphology. This review synthesizes findings on shallow and deep cryogenic effects, linking phase transformation to mechanical and machining performance. It highlights optimization challenges in soaking duration, hybrid treatment integration, and real-time process monitoring guiding sustainable, high-performance manufacturing of Ti-6Al-4V alloy components.
